files.README.md:
# rust-sql-mysql-decided-offset-optional-repository-commits

Data access layer generated by [DB2CRUD](https://github.com/RaulEstevezA/DB2CRUD) for a database that already exists: plain entities, repositories with their own SQL through sqlx 0.9.1 and services, in asynchronous Rust. It does not create or migrate the database, and it depends on no web framework.

## Settings

- Database: mysql.
- Entities: written for the tables the input had no type for.
- Services: take and return the entities; updates take an Option<Option<T>> per field: None when not sent, Some(None) to empty it; errors are `Result<T, DomainError>`.
- Transactions: every repository write is committed at once.
- Lists: lists return pages by offset and limit.

## Layout

```text
src/database.rs          the connection of DATABASE_URL
src/unit_of_work.rs      the repositories of every table, and the transactions
src/errors.rs            DomainError: NotFound, Conflict, ValidationFailed, Database; no HTTP codes
src/entities/            one entity per table
src/repositories/        the repositories of each table
src/services/            one service per table
tests/data/              repositories against a database, services on the in-memory repositories
crud-contract.json       what was written, for CRUD2Controller
```

## Running the tests

```bash
TEST_DATABASE_URL="mysql://app:app@localhost:3306/app" cargo test   # a real, disposable database: it is emptied
```

/// A row of the "products" table. The repositories read and write it with SQL; a field stays `None` until it is set or read.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct Product {
    pub id: Option<i64>,
    pub category_id: Option<i64>,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub price: Option<rust_decimal::Decimal>,
    pub status: Option<String>,
    pub version: Option<i32>,
    pub deleted_at: Option<chrono::DateTime<chrono::FixedOffset>>,
}
